title.en: The Spine: A Tower That Bends

text.zh: 从背后看，脊柱不是一根直棍，而是侧看前后交替的四道弯。这几道弯是它能扛住你的关键。
text.en: Seen from behind, the spine is no straight rod. From the side it draws four curves alternating front and back — and those curves are why it can carry you.

text.zh: 最上面 7 块是颈椎，最轻也最灵活。你此刻点头、摇头、转头，动的都是它们。
text.en: The top seven are the cervical vertebrae — the lightest and most mobile. Every nod, shake and turn of your head happens here.

text.zh: 往下 12 块胸椎，棘突长得又长又斜，一片压着一片，像屋顶的瓦。稳固是有代价的——这一段几乎扭不动。
text.en: Next come twelve thoracic vertebrae, their spines long and steeply angled, overlapping like roof tiles. Stability comes at a price: this is the least mobile stretch of the whole spine.

text.zh: 再往下只剩 5 块腰椎，却要接住上半身的全部重量，所以它们长得又厚又宽。
text.en: Only five lumbar vertebrae remain below, yet they must catch the entire weight of the upper body — which is why they are built so thick and broad.

text.zh: 重量最后压在骶骨上。它由 5 块椎骨长死成一整块，左右两面卡进髋骨——从这里往下，一条脊柱就变成了两条腿。
text.en: The load finally rests on the sacrum. Five vertebrae have fused into one solid wedge, locked into the hip bones on either side — from here down, one spine becomes two legs.

text.zh: 从颈椎到腰椎，几乎每两块椎骨之间都垫着一片椎间盘。它们加起来约占脊柱长度的四分之一，弯腰的角度全靠它们让出来。
text.en: From the neck down to the lower back, almost every two vertebrae have a disc between them. Together they make up roughly a quarter of the spine's length, and every degree of bending is borrowed from them.

text.zh: 这座塔是空心的。椎孔连成一条管道，脊髓就住在里面——脊柱的形状，本来就是为了护住它。
text.en: The tower is hollow. The vertebral openings line up into a canal and the spinal cord lives inside it — the whole shape of the spine exists to protect that cord.

text.zh: 光靠骨头它立不住。两侧的竖脊肌把每一节都往回拽，脊柱才不会像一摞积木那样散开。
text.en: Bone alone cannot hold it upright. The erector spinae on either side pull every segment back into line, so the spine never scatters like a stack of blocks.

text.zh: 一节骨、一片软垫，外面再箍上两条肌肉。少哪一样，你都既撑不住体重，也弯不下腰。
text.en: A block of bone, a cushion between, and two ropes of muscle lashed around the outside. Take away any one of them and you can neither hold your weight nor bend at all.
